items.stem: What is meant by “substrate-level phosphorylation”?
items.answer: Direct synthesis of ATP from a high-energy substrate, as in the conversion of PEP to pyruvic acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: direct synthesis of ATP from a high-energy substrate, as in the conversion of PEP to pyruvic acid.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about glycolysis and fermentation is correct?
items.answer: In fermentation, less than seven per cent of the energy in glucose is released.
items.markingKey: (a) In fermentation, less than seven per cent of the energy in glucose is released. The other statements are false. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm. Glycolysis is common to aerobic and anaerobic respiration and does not need oxygen. Yeast converts pyruvic acid to CO₂ and ethanol; lactic acid is formed in muscles and some bacteria.
options: In fermentation, less than seven per cent of the energy in glucose is released.
In alcoholic fermentation, pyruvic acid is converted to lactic acid.
Glycolysis occurs in the mitochondria.
Glycolysis requires oxygen.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Fermentation releases most of the energy stored in glucose.
Reason (R): Yeasts poison themselves to death when the alcohol concentration reaches about 13 per cent.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Less than 7% of the energy in glucose is released and not all of it is trapped as ATP. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In alcoholic fermentation, pyruvic acid is converted to lactic acid.”
items.answer: Yeast converts pyruvic acid to CO₂ and ethanol; lactic acid is formed in muscles and some bacteria.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Yeast converts pyruvic acid to CO₂ and ethanol; lactic acid is formed in muscles and some bacteria.

items.stem: Distinguish between alcoholic and lactic acid fermentation on three points.
items.answer: Alcoholic – in yeast; pyruvic acid → CO₂ + ethanol; enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase; CO₂ released. Lactic acid – in muscles and some bacteria; pyruvic acid → lactic acid; enzyme lactate dehydrogenase; no CO₂ released.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
A pathway of glucose breakdown has these features: occurs in muscles during vigorous exercise and in some bacteria; pyruvic acid reduced to lactic acid; enzyme lactate dehydrogenase.
(i) Identify the pathway. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were aerobic respiration? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Lactic acid fermentation (ii) no CO₂ released (iii) Krebs cycle and ETS in mitochondria; requires O₂
items.markingKey: (i) lactic acid fermentation – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: no CO₂ released – 1 mark. (iii) for aerobic respiration: requires O₂; complete oxidation of glucose to CO₂ and H₂O; Krebs cycle and ETS in mitochondria – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which term describes the breaking of C–C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within cells, leading to release of energy?
items.answer: respiration
items.markingKey: (b) Respiration: the breaking of C–C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within cells, leading to release of energy.
options: substrate-level phosphorylation
respiration
fermentation
lactic acid fermentation

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of glycolysis: pyruvic acid, 3-phosphoglyceric acid, 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate. Give a reason.
items.answer: 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate → 3-phosphoglyceric acid → pyruvic acid
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate → 3-phosphoglyceric acid → pyruvic acid; 1 mark for the reason: EMP pathway as in NCERT.

items.stem:
At a bakery in Kolkata, dough left with yeast becomes soft and spongy, and a faint smell of alcohol is noticed.
(i) Name the process. (1 mark)
(ii) Name the products formed from pyruvic acid. (1 mark)
(iii) Why does this process yield little energy? Name the enzymes involved. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Alcoholic fermentation. (ii) CO₂ (makes dough spongy) and ethanol. (iii) Glucose is only partially oxidised; net gain 2 ATP; enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase.

items.stem: What is meant by “respiration”?
items.answer: The breaking of C–C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within cells, leading to release of energy.

items.stem: A pathway of glucose breakdown has these features: complete oxidation of glucose to CO₂ and H₂O; Krebs cycle and ETS in mitochondria; requires O₂. Identify the pathway. Give a reason.
items.answer: Aerobic respiration

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: What is meant by “electron transport system (ETS)”?
items.answer: The metabolic pathway in the inner mitochondrial membrane through which electrons pass from one carrier to another.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the metabolic pathway in the inner mitochondrial membrane through which electrons pass from one carrier to another.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about aerobic respiration: the Krebs cycle and the electron transport system is correct?
items.answer: The Krebs cycle takes place in the matrix of mitochondria.
items.markingKey: (c) The Krebs cycle takes place in the matrix of mitochondria. The other statements are false. Oxygen is the final acceptor; it combines with electrons and H⁺ to form water. F₀ forms the proton channel; F₁ synthesises ATP. One turn gives 1 ATP (GTP) by substrate-level phosphorylation, besides 3 NADH and 1 FADH₂.
options: The F₀ part of ATP synthase synthesises ATP.
Oxygen is the first electron acceptor of the ETS.
The Krebs cycle takes place in the matrix of mitochondria.
One turn of the Krebs cycle produces 3 ATP directly.

the electron transport system

items.stem: How many molecules of CO₂ are produced in the Krebs cycle from 4 molecules of acetyl CoA?
items.markingKey: (a) Each turn (one acetyl CoA) gives 3 NADH₂, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP and 2 CO₂; one glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA. 4 turn(s) × 2 = 8.

items.stem:
A poison such as cyanide blocks complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) of the mitochondria in a patient admitted to a hospital in Ranchi.
(i) What is the normal role of complex IV? (1 mark)
(ii) What would happen to ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation? (1 mark)
(iii) Explain why the Krebs cycle would also slow down. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) It passes electrons to O₂, the final acceptor, forming water. (ii) It would stop because electron flow and proton pumping stop. (iii) NADH and FADH₂ can no longer be oxidised, so NAD⁺ and FAD are not regenerated for the Krebs cycle reactions.

items.stem: How many molecules of NADH₂ (NADH + H⁺) are produced in the Krebs cycle from 6 molecules of acetyl CoA?
items.markingKey: (b) Each turn (one acetyl CoA) gives 3 NADH₂, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP and 2 CO₂; one glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA. 6 turn(s) × 3 = 18.

items.stem: Give two differences between the Krebs cycle and the electron transport system.
items.answer: The Krebs cycle: produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP per turn; occurs in the mitochondrial matrix. The electron transport system: O₂ is the final acceptor; electrons pass through complexes I to IV.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the Krebs cycle – produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP per turn; occurs in the mitochondrial matrix; the electron transport system – O₂ is the final acceptor; electrons pass through complexes I to IV.

items.stem: Describe the Krebs cycle and the electron transport system. How is ATP formed in oxidative phosphorylation?
items.answer: Acetyl CoA + OAA + H₂O → citric acid (citrate synthase); isomerised to isocitrate; two decarboxylations → α-ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA; succinyl CoA → succinic acid (GTP/ATP); OAA regenerated; per turn 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 ATP, 2 CO₂. ETS: NADH → complex I → ubiquinone; FADH₂ → complex II → ubiquinone; → complex III → cytochrome c → complex IV → O₂ + H⁺ → water. Proton gradient; H⁺ flows through F₀ of complex V; F₁ synthesises ATP; 3 ATP per NADH, 2 per FADH₂.
items.markingKey: 2 marks Krebs; 2 marks ETS; 1 mark oxidative phosphorylation.

items.stem: Define the term “oxidative decarboxylation”.
items.answer: The conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA by pyruvic dehydrogenase, releasing CO₂ and NADH.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA by pyruvic dehydrogenase, releasing CO₂ and NADH.

items.stem: Give three differences between the electron transport system and oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate.
items.answer: The electron transport system: located in the inner mitochondrial membrane; electrons pass through complexes I to IV; forms water. Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate: catalysed by pyruvic dehydrogenase; needs coenzyme A and NAD⁺; occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. the electron transport system – located in the inner mitochondrial membrane; electrons pass through complexes I to IV; forms water; oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate – catalysed by pyruvic dehydrogenase; needs coenzyme A and NAD⁺; occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about aerobic respiration: the Krebs cycle and the electron transport system is correct?

options: The ETS is located in the matrix of the mitochondrion.
The F₀ part of ATP synthase synthesises ATP.
Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl CoA in the cytoplasm.
Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents from both FADH₂ and NADH.

items.stem:
In a seed germination experiment in Mysuru, germinating groundnut seeds released 70 mL of CO₂ while consuming 100 mL of O₂, and germinating wheat grains released 50 mL of CO₂ while consuming 50 mL of O₂.
(i) Calculate the RQ for each. (2 marks)
(ii) Identify the main respiratory substrate in each. (1 mark)
(iii) Why is the RQ of fats less than 1? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Groundnut 70/100 = 0.7; wheat 50/50 = 1. (ii) Groundnut – fats; wheat – carbohydrates (starch). (iii) Fats contain less oxygen relative to carbon and hydrogen, so more O₂ is needed than CO₂ released.
